chapters.summary: In the Dandaka forest Rama promises to protect the sages. At Panchavati he defeats Khara's army, but Ravana, warned in vain by Maricha, sends the golden deer. Sita is carried off; the dying Jatayu tells Rama, and Shabari points the way to Sugriva.

signs.text: East: Panchavati, by the river Godavari.
Panchavati: the place of the five banyan trees, by the Godavari.
East: the deep forest. North: Janasthana. South, across the river: the road to Pampa.
East: Lake Pampa and the hermitage of Matanga.
East: the hill of Rishyamuka, where Sugriva lives in hiding.

then.say: The forest of Dandaka: vast, ancient, and full of danger. Hermitages shelter in its clearings, and night-wanderers roam between them.
Stay close, Sita. Lakshmana, keep your bow ready.
I am not afraid, as long as we are together.

then.objective: Find the hermitage of the Dandaka sages.

then.say: Panchavati lies east, by the Godavari. May you live there in peace.

else.say: Rama! We have heard of you, even here. Look at us: we are old and few. The night-wanderers of Janasthana hunt us like deer.
We do not ask for wealth. We ask for protection. You are the king's son; protect us.
Revered sages, I came to the forest to keep my father's word. Now I have a second reason. I will protect you, as long as I live here.

then.say: Rama, these rakshasas have done us no harm. Must you fight them?
I have given my word to the sages, Sita. I would sooner give up my life.

else.say: Then go to Panchavati, by the Godavari, as the sage Agastya advised. Live there, and the forest will be safer for it.
The sages give you a healing herb.

else.objective: Travel east through the forest to Panchavati.

then.say: The tall kusha grass here is thick with night-wanderers. Do not walk through it unless you are ready to fight.
The tall kusha grass here is thick with night-wanderers, but they fear Rama's bow and stay hidden. Walk on in peace.

cmds.say: Our shrine is open to you. Rest there before you go on. Each verse you restore makes your heroes stronger.
Even here, a trader finds a way! Fruit, roots, honey and herbs.
The sages' hermitage is north of here, in a clearing. They have been hoping someone would come.
Another hermit to frighten? No... a prince with a bow. Then fight me!

battle.intro: A night-wanderer of the Dandaka forest attacks!

onWin.say: The night-wanderer vanishes into the trees, leaving fruit behind.

cmds.say: The sages of this forest need us. Let us find their hermitage first.

cmds.objective: Find the hermitage of the Dandaka sages.

then.say: Panchavati: five great banyan trees beside the Godavari. Lakshmana builds a fine hut of leaves and bamboo, and the seasons turn in peace.
Do not be alarmed, children. I am Jatayu, king of the vultures, and a friend of your father, King Dasharatha.
When you go out into the forest, I will watch over Sita.
Thank you, friend of my father. We are honoured.
One day, Surpanakha, sister of Ravana, sees Rama and wants him for herself. Rama gently refuses, and Lakshmana drives her away when she turns on Sita.
Wounded and furious, she flees to her brother Khara at Janasthana. Now an army of night-wanderers is gathering to the north.

then.objective: Face Khara's army at Janasthana, north of Panchavati.

cmds.say: Thick thorn bushes block the way north.
I am old, but my eyes are sharp. Nothing moves in this forest that I do not see.

then.say: They say even Maricha, Rama's old enemy, warned Ravana: 'Rama is dharma in bodily form, good, and true in his valour.'
{w:vigrahavat} means "having a body". Think of it: {w:dharma} itself, walking among us in bark cloth.
But the forest to the east glitters strangely at dusk. Be careful of things that seem too beautiful.

else.say: The Godavari is gentle here. But the forest to the east glitters strangely at dusk. Be careful of things that seem too beautiful.

cmds.say: I keep the shrine of Panchavati. Rest, save, or recite: it is open to all.

then.say: Rama is {w:dharma} (righteousness) in human form. Now that verse is a mantra for Rama himself.

then.objective: Return to the hut. Something golden glimmers among the trees...

else.say: The verse is whole. Keep it close; you will need its strength.
You have heard a terrible warning, spoken far away by the sea. Even a night-wanderer knew what Rama is. Recite it for me, so that it is whole.

then.say: Rama is {w:dharma} (righteousness) in human form. Now that verse is a mantra for Rama himself.

then.objective: Return to the hut. Something golden glimmers among the trees...

else.say: Not yet whole. Look at the verse card again and recite it once more.
Come back when you are ready.

then.say: Lakshmana is with me. Go, and come back soon.
A {w:mrga} (deer) of pure gold, dappled with silver and jewels, steps out from the trees near the hut.

then.choice: Sita asks: "{player}, what is that, among the trees?"

options.label: It is there, among the trees.

then.say: Yes, there. But what is it?
Lakshmana sees it too. But what is it?
Rama, look! I have never seen anything so beautiful.
Brother, no deer is made of gold. I think it is Maricha, in disguise. He has led many hunters to their death.
If it is Maricha, I will deal with him; if it is a real deer, Sita shall have it. Lakshmana, guard Sita. Do not leave her for anything.
I will not leave her side, brother.

onCorrect.say: Yes, that is what I said. Go carefully, Rama.

onWrong.say: The verse card shows each word, {player}. Go carefully, Rama.

then.say: Lakshmana stays behind to guard Sita. Rama takes up his bow and follows the deer.

then.objective: Follow the golden deer east into the forest.

then.say: Rama has been quiet since Janasthana. He says a storm is coming.
The sage by the shrine asked for you, {player}.

then.objective: Recite Maricha's warning with the sage at the shrine.

else.say: The banyans give such cool shade. This is the happiest home we have had in the forest.

cmds.say: I will guard Sita with my life, brother. Go after the deer, but come back quickly.
The golden deer looks back at you, then bounds away between the trees.

then.say: The forest to the east is dense and strangely quiet. There is no reason to go there yet.
A whisper on the wind, Valmiki's voice: "Restore the verse you heard by the sea first, child. The sage at the shrine will hear you."

then.objective: Recite Maricha's warning with the sage at the shrine.

else.say: Sita is calling from the hut.

cmds.say: The Godavari runs deep here. There is no need to cross it yet.
Drums thunder across the camp. Fourteen thousand night-wanderers stand ready, and at their head stand Khara and Dushana.
Stand with me, Lakshmana. We fight for the sages of the forest.
Khara will crush you! He has never lost a battle! But first you must get past me!

onWin.say: The night-wanderer flees into the dark.

cmds.say: Hermits in our camp? I will show you the strength of Janasthana!

battle.intro: A sentry of Khara's camp attacks!

onWin.say: The sentry drops a pouch of roots as he runs.

then.say: The camp is silent now.

else.say: So these are the hermits who wounded my sister! Dushana, we will finish them together.

else.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

battle.intro: Dushana and Khara lead the army of Janasthana!

onWin.say: Dushana falls, and then Khara himself. The army of Janasthana is scattered like dry leaves in the wind.
The sages of the forest come out to bless Rama. Sita embraces him with joy.
Far away, one survivor reaches Lanka and tells Ravana everything. Ravana listens, and a plan forms: he will carry off Rama's wife.
He flies to the hermitage of Maricha by the sea. Maricha, who once was flung into the ocean by Rama's weapon, turns pale.
Ravana, do not do this! I have seen Rama. Listen to me.
He is {w:dharma} itself. If you take his wife, Lanka will burn.
But Ravana will not listen. He commands Maricha to help him, on pain of death.

onCorrect.say: Even his enemies know what my brother is.

onWrong.say: Look at the verse card again, {player}. Even his enemies know what my brother is.

onWin.objective: Return to Panchavati. Recite Maricha's warning with the sage at the shrine.

cmds.say: A flash of gold between the trees! The deer leaps away, just out of reach.
The deer stops and looks back, as if waiting. When you come near, it is gone again.
The forest grows strange. Some of the deer around you are only shadows. Rama grips his bow.

cmds.objective: Catch up with the golden deer at the far end of the forest.

then.say: Only trampled grass remains.

else.say: The golden deer stands still at last, in the middle of the clearing.
Enough. Show yourself!

else.choice: Rest and save before the battle?

battle.intro: The golden deer is Maricha in disguise!

then.say: Struck by Rama's arrow, the deer falls. There lies Maricha, in his true form.
"Ha Sita! Ha Lakshmana!"
Then Maricha dies. But his cry, in Rama's own voice, rings on through the forest.

else.say: Struck by Rama's arrow, Maricha takes his true form. With his last breath he cries out in Rama's own voice: "Ha Sita! Ha Lakshmana!"

onWin.say: Lakshmana was right. That cry will reach Sita. What will she think? We must hurry back!
On the way, Rama meets Lakshmana running toward him.
Brother! Sita heard the cry and begged me to go to you. When I would not, she said terrible things. I had to come.
You left her alone? Quickly, Lakshmana!
Lakshmana rejoins your party.
The hut is empty. Flowers lie scattered on the ground. Sita is gone.
Sita! Sita!

then.say: As Ravana carried her off through the sky, Sita had called out to the trees.
Now Rama goes from tree to tree and asks each one.
The trees cannot answer. The Godavari is silent too: she fears Ravana.
Nearby, a herd of deer is resting. They look at Rama again and again.
Where is Sita? Tell me!
The deer rise at once. They face south, toward the sky where Sita was taken, and run to the river, looking back at Rama.
Brother, the deer are showing us the way. South, across the river!

else.say: Rama searches every grove and riverbank, calling her name. The trees and the river give no answer.
Brother, look: broken flowers, and marks on the ground leading south, across the river.

onWin.objective: Search for Sita. Cross the Godavari to the south.

then.say: Only feathers remain in the quiet glade.

else.say: In a clearing, among the broken pieces of a great chariot, lies Jatayu, king of the vultures, gravely wounded.
Jatayu! Friend of my father, what has happened?
Rama... {w:ayushmat} (long-lived one), listen to me.

then.choice: Jatayu has breath for only a few words. What will you ask him?

options.label: Which way did he take her?

else.choice: Jatayu has breath for only a few words. What will you ask him?

then.choice: Jatayu has breath for only a few words. What will you ask him?

options.label: Which way did he take her?

then.say: Ravana. The king of the rakshasas.
Through the sky... to the south.
Jatayu only gasps. His breath is almost gone.

else.say: It was Ravana. He took Sita in his flying chariot and flew south. I broke his chariot and fought him with all my strength.
But I am old, and he struck me down. She cried out your name, Rama. Go south. You will find her.
With these words, Jatayu, faithful friend of Dasharatha, gives up his life in Rama's arms.

then.say: Lakshmana, this bird gave his life for us.

else.say: Rama himself performs the last rites for Jatayu, as he would for his own father.
He gave his life for Sita. We will not forget him.

cmds.say: Something lies in the clearing ahead. You cannot pass by.

then.say: The hollow is peaceful now.

else.say: A huge, headless form blocks the hollow. Its long arms sweep the ground, catching anything that comes near. This is Kabandha.

options.label: Rest and save, then face him

battle.intro: Kabandha seizes the princes in his long arms!

onWin.say: Rama and Lakshmana cut free of Kabandha's arms. His curse is broken, and a shining celestial rises from the hollow.
Thank you, Rama. I was cursed to take that form until you came. Hear my advice.
Go to Lake Pampa, where the holy woman Shabari waits for you. Then find Sugriva, the vanara, on Rishyamuka hill. He will help you find Sita.
You received 2 healing herbs.

else.say: You step back quietly.

then.say: Lake Pampa: clear water, lotuses of every colour, and the old hermitage of the sage Matanga on its shore.
Shabari's seat by the hermitage is empty, but her flowers still bloom.

else.say: An old woman in bark garments rises to greet them, her eyes full of light. She is Shabari, the last disciple of the sage Matanga.
Rama! My teachers told me you would come, and that I must wait for you. I have waited all these years.
Now that I have seen you, my life is complete. Please accept these fruits. I gathered them from the forest for you.
Your devotion honours us, Shabari.
Go to Rishyamuka hill, east of here. Sugriva the vanara lives there in hiding, with four companions. He will help you find Sita.
Then, with Rama's blessing, Shabari enters the sacred fire and rises, radiant, to the world of her teachers.
Brother, we have a path now. Sugriva will help us.
Then we go to Rishyamuka. Sita, we are coming.
So ends the third book, the Book of the Forest.

else.objective: Go east to Rishyamuka hill to begin Book 4.

cmds.say: Shabari is waiting for us at the hermitage, brother. Let us see her first.
Pilgrims come to Pampa from everywhere. I sell what they need.
The flowers the sage Matanga's students wore never fade, they say. Rest at our shrine. It is a place of great peace.
There are monkeys on the hill to the east! Big ones! They watch everyone who comes to the lake.
Deep in the kusha grass, a sage has hidden a chest of healing herbs.
You found 1 healing herb.

then.say: The tree is quiet now. A few petals still fall.

else.say: Petals fall from a tree beside the hut. It saw everything.
Sita asked the trees and the river to tell Rama. The river was afraid. But the trees remember her words.
